findings.title: Team scope condition always includes OR branch even with no users
findings.body: buildTeamAuthorizationCondition only pushes the userId OR condition when userIdsFromTeam.length > 0, but previously the WHERE-based implementation always included a userId IN [] clause (effectively false). The Prisma.sql version silently omits the userId clause entirely when it's empty, resulting in only the team booking condition applying—functionally fine here, but note that if usersFromTeam is empty while teamId condition is also false, there is no NOTHING fallback, which is still consistent. However, the subtle risk is that this branch previously using findAllByTeamIds for all orgs can return huge arrays bound as ANY($1) parameters—confirm Prisma supports array binding for ANY() cleanly across drivers (postgres only); this breaks compatibility if any other DB target is used.

findings.title: Potential unbounded growth of ANY() array for large orgs
findings.body: buildOrgAuthorizationCondition fetches all teams and all users of an org and inlines them into an ANY($ids) SQL array. For large organizations this could produce very large parameter arrays in raw SQL queries, which may hit Postgres parameter limits or cause performance degradation compared to a JOIN/subquery based condition in the previous Prisma object query.

findings.title: Removed caching tests not replaced
findings.body: The PR removes the previous 'Caching' describe block tests (that verified getAuthorizationConditions/getFilterConditions caching behavior) without adding equivalent coverage for the new Prisma.sql-based caching. Since cachedAuthConditions/cachedFilterConditions are still implemented in the service, this leaves caching behavior untested.

findings.title: findMany API no longer tested
findings.body: The original test exercised service.findMany(...), the public querying API consumers would use. The rewritten test only calls getBaseConditions() and performs a manual $queryRaw, meaning the actual integration of baseConditions into a real repository/service query method (if such method still exists elsewhere) is no longer verified by this test file.
